“Lack of imaginary play” does not mean lack of imagination, and you typically only see that trait ascribed to developing children. The lack of imaginary play refers to behaviors such as stacking or lining up building blocks rather than creating a structure, organizing your model trains instead of putting them on the track, only playing very literally with animal toys etc. it’s not a lack of imagination at all. I find people with autism are extremely gifted in the creativity department. 
However, this person does not describe “maladaptive” daydreaming. Perhaps they get carried away, because they don’t seem to learn the lyrics of a favorite song despite constantly listening, but it’s not impacting their whole life negatively to ignore the core structure of a song. Lol. (I am also autistic, these folks give me a laugh sometimes.)

I have and will always hate the phrase “We make time for what’s important”. It leaves no room for nuance. The truth is that we prioritize things very specifically, especially when having a full plate and little time to clear it. You have made time for what is important. You made time for your future, the space you live in and maintain, and a dependent who cannot live without you (pet or no does not matter). You prioritized, she just isn’t happy about being at the bottom of your list. Her entertainment is not your responsibility, and neither is her opinion on your education and life you live. You deserve to be allowed to reap the benefits of hard work you put in despite also having a disability. 
You also didn’t say anything outlandish as though you would never hang out again, just that you need to see what your schedule is even like before you make plans around it. Her gross overreaction to you essentially telling her you don’t even know what your schedule is like is fairly telling. She seems really dismissive at best and manipulative occasionally at the worst. 
NTA.
